title: Confidence Intervals for the Mean (Large Samples)

questions.feedbackIfWrong: The sample mean $\bar{x}$ is the best point estimate of $\mu$.
questions.prompt: Which of the following is the best point estimate of the population mean $\mu$?
hints: It's the statistic you compute directly from the sample data.
It's an unbiased estimator of $\mu$.

questions.feedbackIfWrong: The critical value for 95% confidence is $z_c = 1.96$.
hints: This z‑score leaves 2.5% in each tail of the standard normal distribution.
It is approximately 2.
questions.prompt: For a 95% confidence level, the critical value $z_c$ is ___.
If $n=100$, $s=10$, and $z_c=1.96$, what is the margin of error? (Round to two decimals.)
hints: Use $E = z_c \cdot s / \sqrt{n}$.

questions.prompt: What happens to the width of a confidence interval if the sample size increases?
hints: Think about the formula $E = z_c \cdot s / \sqrt{n}$.
A larger $n$ makes the denominator larger.
questions.feedbackIfWrong: As $n$ increases, the margin of error decreases, so the interval becomes narrower.
options: It depends on the confidence level.

questions.prompt: To determine the minimum sample size, a smaller desired margin of error $E$ requires a ___ sample size.
hints: Look at the formula $n = (z_c \sigma / E)^2$.
If $E$ is smaller, the fraction inside the parentheses gets larger.
questions.feedbackIfWrong: A smaller $E$ requires a larger sample size.

questions.prompt: What is the critical value $z_c$ for a 90% confidence interval?
hints: This z‑score leaves 5% in each tail.
It is between 1.6 and 1.7.
The confidence level describes the method, not a single interval.
Once an interval is computed, $\mu$ is either in it or not.
questions.prompt: Which statement correctly interprets a 95% confidence interval for $\mu$?
options: There is a 95% chance that $\mu$ lies in this specific interval.
If we repeat the sampling many times, about 95% of the intervals will contain $\mu$.
95% of the sample data lie within the interval.
The sample mean has a 95% probability of being exactly $\mu$.
questions.feedbackIfWrong: The correct interpretation: about 95% of all samples will produce intervals that contain $\mu$.

questions.prompt: A confidence interval is centered at the ___ mean.
hints: It's the statistic we use as the point estimate.
Denoted by $\bar{x}$.
questions.feedbackIfWrong: The interval is centered at the sample mean.

questions.prompt: A sample of size 50 has mean 100 and standard deviation 15. Compute the margin of error for 95% confidence. (Round to one decimal.)
Which of the following would produce a narrower confidence interval?
hints: A smaller margin of error makes the interval narrower.
Look at $E = z_c \cdot \sigma / \sqrt{n}$: reducing $\sigma$ reduces $E$.
questions.feedbackIfWrong: Decreasing $\sigma$ reduces the margin of error, giving a narrower interval.
The margin of error is $z_c$ times the standard error.
hints: It's $\sigma / \sqrt{n}$ or $s / \sqrt{n}$.
It's often called the standard deviation of the sampling distribution.
questions.prompt: The margin of error $E$ is the product of the critical value and the ___ error of the mean.

hints: The margin of error is half the width of the interval.
questions.prompt: If a confidence interval is (25, 35), what is the margin of error?

questions.feedbackIfWrong: 99% confidence gives the widest interval because $z_c = 2.575$ is the largest.
hints: A higher confidence level requires a larger critical value $z_c$.
The critical value is largest for the highest confidence.
options: All intervals have the same width.
questions.prompt: For a fixed sample size and standard deviation, which confidence level yields the widest interval?

questions.feedbackIfWrong: The function returns the margin of error.
questions.prompt: In Google Sheets, the function `=CONFIDENCE.NORM(alpha, sd, n)` returns the ___ of error.
hints: It's the same $E$ we add and subtract from $\bar{x}$.
Not the interval width.

questions.prompt: How large a sample is needed to estimate $\mu$ within 2 units with 95% confidence if $\sigma=10$? (Round up to nearest integer.)
